title.narrative: Strengthening National and Regional Mine Action Capacity in Lebanon through the LMAC

description.narrative: Lebanon continues to face a significant humanitarian and development challenge arising from widespread ExplosiveOrdnance (EO) contamination resulting from successive conflicts, sharply exacerbated by the 2024 conflict. EOcontamination continues to pose serious risks to civilian populations, restricts humanitarian access, delays safereturn and reconstruction, and undermines agricultural livelihoods and environmental recovery, particularly in SouthLebanon and other conflict-affected areas. At the same time, national institutions responsible for humanitarianmine action are operating under exceptional pressure due to a protracted economic crisis, staff attrition, and thelessening of international enabling capacity and operations with the withdrawal of UNIFIL at end of 2026, increasingthe urgency of a nationally led, sustainable response.The Lebanon Mine Action Centre (LMAC), operating under the Ministry of National Defence (MoD) as part of theLebanese Armed Forces (LAF), remains the nationally mandated authority responsible for coordinating, regulating,and overseeing all humanitarian mine action in the country. While substantial progress has been achieved over thepast decade with UNDP support, the scale and complexity of renewed EO contamination —including in rubble anddebris environments— require strengthened institutional capacity and scaled-up, adaptive operations to sustainhumanitarian impact and ensure continued compliance with international obligations in a post-UNIFIL operatingenvironment.This project aims to strengthen LMAC’s institutional leadership and systems, scale up safe and effective humanitarianmine action operations, and reinforce people-centered approaches to risk education and victim assistance.
